metadata.name: 16.1.a Percentage of persons who believe that Poland is a safe place to live
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Increase in effectiveness of the state and its institutions for social and economic enhancement and inclusion
metadata.definition: Percentage of respondents who answered affirmatively to the question: 'In your opinion, is Poland a safe place to live?'.
metadata.methodology: The indicator comes from the survey Current problems and events conducted on a randomly selected group of approximately 1000 residents of Poland. Possible answers were: Yes; No; It is hard to say.

metadata.name: 16.1.b Percentage of persons who declare trust in public institutions - local authorities of cities or gminas
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Increase in effectiveness of the state and its institutions for social and economic enhancement and inclusion
metadata.definition: Percentage of respondents who answered affirmatively to the question: Generally speaking, do you have or do not you have confidence in local authorities of the city or the gmina?
metadata.methodology: Respondents were shown a list of 23 different entities and institutions acting in the country, as well as international organizations, including the Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity, the Polish Red Cross, the Caritas, the Army, the Scouting, the Roman Catholic Church, The Police, the Ombudsman, Local authorities of a city/a gmina, the European Union, the NATO, the UN, the Institute of National Remembrance, Courts, Officials of public administration, the Television, the Government, Large companies, Newspapers, Churches of other denominations, Trade unions, the Sejm and the Senate, and Political parties. The indicator includes answers: I definitely have confidence and I rather have confidence. Possible answers were: I definitely have confidence; I rather have confidence; I do not rather have confidence; I definitely do not have confidence; It is hard to say. The indicator comes from the survey Current problems and events conducted on a randomly selected group of approximately 1000 adult residents of Poland.

metadata.name: 16.1.c Number of legal cases resolved in the first instance per 100 thousand population
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Increase in effectiveness of the state and its institutions for social and economic enhancement and inclusion
metadata.definition: Number of cases resolved in first instance courts (criminal cases and other than criminal (non-criminal) cases) expressed per 100 thous. population.
metadata.methodology: The indicator measures judicial activity of courts in relation to the population.The numerator comprises criminal cases and non-criminal cases resolved by courts of first instance. The denominator is the total population. The indicator is expressed per 100 thous. population.Data on the number of resolved court cases are derived from administrative justice records. Population data are provided by Eurostat based on data supplied by the statistical offices of Member States.Criminal and non-criminal cases are defined according to the methodology of the European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ).A case resolved at first instance is a case completed by judgment or other decision in the reference year that terminates proceedings at first-instance level.

metadata.name: 16.2.a Regulatory quality
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Improvement in legislation quality and application of law
metadata.definition: Perceptions of the ability of the government to formulate and implement sound policies and regulations that permit and promote private sector development.
metadata.methodology: Regulatory quality is one of the six good governance indicators, so called Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI). The other good governance indicators include: voice and accountability, political stability and absence of violence/ terrorism, government effectiveness, rule of law and control of corruption. The six aggregate indicators range from -2.5 to 2.5, with higher values corresponding to better governance.

metadata.name: 16.3.a Share of expenditures on national defense in GDP
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Integrated national security management, including state defense management and building adaptive capabilities
metadata.definition: Sum of expenditures  on  national defense in relations to GDP.
metadata.methodology: Defense expenditures are the total amount of expenditures incurred in a reporting year expressed according to the methodology of preparation of “Defense Planning Capability Survey – DPCS”. Gross domestic product (GDP) illustrates the final result of the activity of all entities of the national economy (resident producer units – domestic) in a given year. The exact definition and methodology for calculating GDP is contained in the regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013 on the European system of national and regional accounts in the European Union (ESA 2010). For the purposes of monitoring, the actual expenditure incurred for national defense calculated after the reporting year has been taken into account.

metadata.name: 16.4.a Enterprises using the e-Delivery service
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Wider use of ICT for state governance and communication with its citizens (including entrepreneurs)
metadata.definition: Enterprises using the registered electronic delivery service (e-Delivery).
metadata.methodology: Information on enterprises’ use of e-Delivery, i.e. registered electronic delivery services, is derived from the SSI-01 survey report: “Report on the use of information and communication technologies in enterprises”. The survey covers the use of ICT within enterprises. It is not relevant whether the ICT equipment or software used by the enterprise is owned by the enterprise or not.The term ICT refers to information and communication technologies that process, store and transmit information in electronic form. These technologies include the Internet and other computer networks, information systems, computers and other computing devices.The SSI-01 questionnaire is completed by legal persons, organisational units without legal personality, and natural persons conducting economic activity with 10 or more persons employed, and whose activity is classified, according to the Polish Classification of Activities (PKD), under sections A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, L, M, N, R and S.The e-Delivery service is the electronic equivalent of a registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt. Through this service, public entities, citizens and businesses can use convenient and secure electronic delivery services that are legally equivalent to traditional registered mail. The e-Delivery service enables official correspondence to be conducted via the Internet, making the process faster and more efficient.

metadata.name: 16.4.b Percentage of individuals using the Internet for contacts with public administration
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Wider use of ICT for state governance and communication with its citizens (including entrepreneurs)
metadata.definition: Proportion of individuals aged 16–74 using the internet to interact with public administration for private purposes (within the last 12 months).
metadata.methodology: The data are derived from the survey Information Society Indicators, which is a sample-based survey conducted using direct interview methods, with voluntary participation. The survey is carried out in April each year. In accordance with requirements specified in European Commission regulations, the survey covers households (with at least one person aged 16–74) located throughout the entire country, as well as all individuals aged 16–74 within those households. The survey does not cover persons living in collective living quarters, such as student dormitories, workers’ hostels, social welfare homes, religious institutions, hospitals, military barracks, prisons, and similar establishments. Foreign nationals may participate in the survey provided that they have sufficient knowledge of the Polish language.The concept of ‘public administration’ refers both to institutions providing public services and to those performing administrative functions. These include, inter alia, tax authorities, customs authorities, registration authorities (e.g. the National Court Register (KRS) and the National Official Business Register (REGON)), social security institutions (e.g. the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS)), public healthcare institutions (e.g. the National Health Fund (NFZ) and hospitals), environmental protection authorities, and other public-sector bodies. Public administration is classified at local, regional, and national levels.Internet-based interaction with public administration includes, inter alia, searching for information on websites, downloading official forms, and submitting completed forms (excluding unsolicited or manually composed email communication).

metadata.name: 16.5.a General government investment rate
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Better use of public resources, including exploitation of EU resources
metadata.definition: Percentage ratio of the nominal value of gross fixed capital formation in general government sector (transaction ESA2010 P.51g) to the nominal value of gross domestic product in a given year.
metadata.methodology: Gross fixed capital formation is the expenditure which increases the value of tangible fixed assets (buildings and structures, machinery, technical equipment and tools, transport equipment and other fixed assets), excluding expenditure comprising the initial investments as well as interest on investment credits and loans for the period of investment realization. The account includes also expenditure on:a) intellectual property products, intended for use for a period longer than 1 year in particular expenditure on research and development and on computer software (purchased and produced for own final use); b) small tools that are used in the production longer than 1 year regardless of their value;c) weapons systems (e.g., tanks, armored vehicles, warships, submarines). General government sector includes the following entities of the national economy:a) entities operating according to principles described in Law on Public finances (budgetary units, appropriated funds and since 2010 also local budgetary establishments, executive agencies and budget institutions as well as until 2005 special funds of budgetary entities, in 2005,2010, own income account of budgetary entities and until 2010, budgetary establishments and auxiliary units of budgetary entities including conducting economic activity ones as well as motivation funds),b) entities for which the financial system was defined in special regulations, and for which the subsidies from the state budget are the main source of financing (public higher educationinstitutions, the Polish Academy of Science and entities established by it, the National Road Fund and other funds managed by Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego, agriculture advisory units and state agencies),c) independent public self-government health care facilities, d) state and local government institutions of culture and national film institutions,e) funds with the legal personality which are connected with state or local government units budgets,f) institutions managing the social security funds (SII, ASIF) and these funds as well as the National Health Fund (in the period 1 I 1999 31 III 2003, health funds),g) public hospitals in the form of limited liability companies and hospitals acting as research institutes (excluded from non-financial corporations sector),h) Bank Guarantee Fund (excluded from financial corporations sector),i) other units, including public corporations and non-commercial institutions that meet ESA 2010 classification criteria to general government sector. Gross domestic product (GDP) illustrates the final result of the activity of all entities of the national economy (resident producer units domestic) in a given year. The exact definition and methodology for calculating GDP is contained in the regulation of the Parliament and of the Council (EU) No 549/2013 of 21 May 2013 on the European system of national and regional accounts in the European Union (ESA 2010). More information on GDP in the profile of the indicator GDP in mln zl.
metadata.notes: The indicator is calculated according to being in force in the countries of the European Union methodology ESA 2010 (European System of National and Regional Accounts), implemented by the regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council (EU) No 549/2013 of 21 May 2013. One of the key changes introduced by ESA 2010 relates to the registration in gross fixed capital formation (not, as previously, in intermediate consumption) the expenditure on research development investment and expenses for small tools , in all institutional sectors, and also expenditure on weapons systems , in the general government sector.

metadata.name: 16.7.a Number of ICT incidents handled by CERT Polska, classified as actual cybersecurity incidents
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Increasing the level of resilience to cyber threats and increasing the level of information protection in the country, as well as promoting knowledge and good practices that enable citizens to better protect their information
metadata.definition: Number of ICT incidents handled by CERT Polska in the reporting year which, after the analysis of reports, were classified as actual cybersecurity incidents and registered as incidents.
metadata.methodology: The indicator is developed on the basis of annual reports on the activities of CERT Polska, published by NASK – National Research Institute. CERT Polska is a team operating within the structures of NASK, established to respond to computer security incidents and performing the tasks of CSIRT NASK.The value of the indicator is determined on the basis of the number of cybersecurity incidents registered by CERT Polska in a given reporting year. The data are derived from the analysis of reports submitted to the team, including via the reporting form and by e-mail. Reports are analysed and grouped, as several reports from different sources may refer to the same incident.The indicator does not include the number of reports itself. The presented value refers to the number of registered incidents, i.e. cases classified, following analysis, as actual cybersecurity incidents.
metadata.source: NASK - National Research Institute / CERT Polska

metadata.name: 16.7.b Percentage of Internet users verifying the accuracy of information or content found on news websites or social media (during the last three months)
metadata.goal: Goal 16. Peace, justice and strong institutions
metadata.priority: Increasing the level of resilience to cyber threats and increasing the level of information protection in the country, as well as promoting knowledge and good practices that enable citizens to better protect their information
metadata.definition: Proportion of respondents to the Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) usage survey who, during the three months preceding the survey, checked the truthfulness of information or content found on online news sites or social media.
metadata.methodology: The indicator measures the extent of actions undertaken by internet users to assess the credibility of information and content found on online news sites or social media.The data required to calculate the indicator are provided by the European Statistical System (ESS), established under Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The ESS constitutes a partnership between Eurostat, national statistical institutes (for example, Statistics Poland), and other national authorities in each Member State responsible for the development, production and dissemination of European statistics.Data are derived from the survey on the use of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in households. This is a representative survey covering persons aged 16–74 living in private households.The numerator is the number of respondents using the internet who undertook actions aimed at assessing the credibility of information or content found online, while the denominator is the total number of respondents using the internet.Actions undertaken to assess the credibility of information or content found online are understood as carrying out at least one of the following activities:a) checking sources or searching online for additional information;b) following or participating in online discussions concerning the information being verified;c) discussing the information being verified with other persons offline or consulting offline sources.
